newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Police vow to arrest prince on return to Cambodia.
newsitem.headline: Police vow to arrest prince on return to Cambodia.

text.p: Cambodian police said on Tuesday they would jail exiled Prince Norodom Sirivudh if he came back to Cambodia, but the prince vowed to return anyway.
Sirivudh was arrested in November 1995 charged with plotting to assassinate Co-Premier Hun Sen.

A month later, he agreed to go into exile in France rather than face trial. He was sentenced in absentia to 10 years' jail in a trial international observers said was a travesty for its shaky charges and lack of evidence.

"The national police declare openly to the national and international public that the office of the national police will take a severe position to implement the court order dated February 22, 1996, which sentenced Prince Norodom Sirivudh to 10 years in prison," read a police declaration dated Tuesday.
Prince Norodom Sirivudh, who has expressed his intention to return to Cambodia, said the declaration would not change his plans.
"I will not change my plans to return to Cambodia," the prince told Reuters in a telephone interview from France.
"I am not so scared," he said.
Sirivudh said he would keep the exact date of his return secret while he finalised his plans.
The declaration, however, appeared to leave an opening for amnesty for Sirivudh, who is the half brother of King Norodom Sihanouk.
It stated that Sihanouk, who has the constitutional power to grant amnesty, could decide to free those convicted of crimes, including Sirivudh.
If proper procedures were followed, the police would then release prisoners, including Sirivudh, the declaration stated.

King Sihanouk said in October that he would grant amnesty to all but the most dangerous prisoners, but under political pressure from groups loyal to Hun Sen, the king later decided not to implement the plan, which would have likely paved the way for Sirivudh's return.
